basics.name: Benjamin Lewis
basics.label: Senior Scientist | Multi-Omic Discovery
basics.summary: Neuro-data scientist specializing in multi-omic biomarker discovery, integrative transcriptomics, and therapeutic target identification in biotech R&D.

work.name: Actio Biosciences
work.summary: Promoted January 2026 in recognition of scientific leadership, cross-program impact, and strategic contributions to portfolio advancement.
highlights: Led multi-omic biomarker discovery and novel target identification across therapeutic programs.
Scientific lead for single-cell and bulk transcriptomic strategy across multiple therapeutic programs.
Designed and deployed a production-grade RNA-seq pipeline (Nextflow, Python, AWS), reducing turnaround from 2 weeks to <48 hours.
Partnered with biology, translational, and executive stakeholders to guide data-driven portfolio decisions.

work.name: Actio Biosciences

work.summary: Cross-functional single-cell and multiomic discovery supporting pipeline and IND-enabling programs.
highlights: Single-cell transcriptomics and multiomics project design and data analysis lead.

work.name: Hardy Diagnostics
work.summary: Developed chromogenic diagnostic media formulations and authored protocols for 510(k) validation studies.

education.summary: Research focused on RNA-binding protein functions in mitochondrial regulation, under the mentorship of Gene Yeo and Tony Hunter.
Stem cell research with extensive molecular biology techniques and stem cell-based disease modeling.

publications.name: LARP4 is an RNA-binding protein that binds nuclear-encoded mitochondrial mRNAs to promote mitochondrial function
publications.summary: Identifies LARP4 as a critical RNA-binding protein regulating nuclear-encoded mitochondrial mRNAs and ensuring proper mitochondrial biogenesis.

publications.name: Autologous and Heterologous Cell Therapy for Hemophilia B toward Functional Restoration of Factor IX
publications.summary: Cell-based therapies for Hemophilia B using corrected iPSCs differentiated into hepatocyte-like cells.

publications.name: Functional Gene Correction for Cystic Fibrosis in Lung Epithelial Cells Generated from Patient iPSCs
publications.summary: CRISPR correction of the CFTR gene mutation in iPSCs from cystic fibrosis patients, restoring normal CFTR expression and function.
